title: The Rabbit Lands Encyclopedia
note: Search all entries by title, topic, material, tool or knowledge. Recipe, spell, book, map and skill pages use the installed game catalogues. The live server decides action eligibility and current prices.

skillNotes.attack: How hard you hit and how often you connect. The server rolls it; the client only shows what it said happened.
skillNotes.defense: How often a blow misses you, and how much of one your armour is allowed to soak.
skillNotes.harvesting: Train by gathering resources. Skill and recommended resource level affect success and timing; tools and carrying capacity also matter.
skillNotes.alchemy: Essences, bars, and the ingredients the rest of the trades are built out of.
skillNotes.magic: Spell unlocks, power and potency depend on Magic level and Magic nexus; family tomes and reagents can also be required.
skillNotes.potion: Everything that ends up in a vial, from the plain healing draught upwards.
skillNotes.summoning: Calling a creature to fight beside you, and the stones and flesh it costs.
skillNotes.manufacturing: Metal work: armour, weapons, and the plates and rings they are made from.
skillNotes.crafting: Rings, medallions and the small worked goods that need a mould.
skillNotes.engineering: Devices and traps, and the tools that build them.
skillNotes.tailoring: Thread, cloth, dye, and every garment made from them.
skillNotes.ranging: Train by ranged combat. Ranging increases maximum distance; shooting remains possible in melee with penalties.
skillNotes.overall: The server tracks overall experience and awards overall levels separately from individual skill levels.

categories.title: The World
categories.summary: Nymara, its hours and its weather
categories.intro: Rabbit Lands takes place on Nymara in the world of Eloria. The server owns world state and the game clock.

entries.title: What the server decides
entries.summary: Actions are checked by the server
entries.body:
The server decides movement, combat, inventory changes, harvesting and trades. The client displays those results and sends your requests.

The encyclopedia combines written guides with installed recipe, spell, book, skill and map catalogues. Those catalogues describe the client build; the live server still decides whether an action is allowed.

entries.title: Day and night
entries.summary: Six real hours to a Nymaran day
entries.body:
A full day is 360 game minutes. At ordinary clock speed one game minute is one real minute, so a Nymaran day lasts six real hours.

Daylight changes creature visibility as well as the scene lighting. See the Almanac tab for the date and current special day.
facts: The clock face on the lower HUD

entries.title: Marks and waypoints
entries.summary: The server's marks and your own
entries.body:
A waypoint is the server's: it appears on your map and reports the distance as you move.

A mark is your own. It never leaves this client, and it is drawn in a different colour so you can tell your own note from something the world told you.

entries.title: Weather and light
entries.summary: Rain, cloud, and the sky over each map
entries.body:
Weather belongs to the map you are standing on. The server states it, the client renders it, and it changes the light rather than only the picture.

An interior does not take the sky's weather. Walking indoors changes what lights you and what you can hear, which is why a doorway can feel like a different time of day.

entries.title: Night visibility and weather
entries.summary: Night changes which creatures you can see
entries.body:
Night reduces the distance at which ordinary creatures become visible. Perception and concealment can also affect visibility. A clear-looking road is not proof that no creature is nearby.

Weather is shared by players on the same map. Outdoor maps can have different weather profiles and changing conditions; interiors without a weather profile do not receive outdoor weather. The Almanac tab describes the current special day and any stated effects.

categories.title: Skills
categories.summary: The thirteen the server keeps for you
categories.intro: The server keeps a level and an experience total for each of these. The Statistics window shows all of them at once; the lower HUD shows the one you asked it to follow.

entries.title: Training skills
entries.summary: Practice, experience and recommended levels
entries.body:
Combat, harvesting, mixing and spellcasting award experience through their own server rules. The Statistics window shows your levels and experience. Spending pick points on attributes, nexus or perks is separate from training a skill.

Recipe levels are recommendations used in success calculations. A listed level does not guarantee a successful mix. Spell pages distinguish an unlock level from a recommended level. Consult the matching recipe or spell for materials, knowledge and nexus requirements.

categories.title: Combat
categories.intro: Combat is entirely the server's. This client asks it to start a fight and then reports what came back.

entries.title: Attacking
entries.summary: Three ways to start a fight
entries.body:
There are three ways to ask for a fight, and all three send the same request.

Hold Alt and click a living creature or player. The move icon on the lower HUD turns into the attack icon while Alt is held, so you can see what a click will do before you make it; let Alt go and it turns back.

Or click the attack icon on the HUD. That latches: the icon stays lit and every click attacks until you choose the move icon again, and holding or releasing Alt does not undo it.

Or select a target and press the attack key.

Whatever you choose, the server walks you into reach, decides whether the fight may start, and refuses the ones that may not.
facts: stays on until you pick the move icon

entries.title: Ranging
entries.summary: Range, reusable ammunition and close combat
entries.body:
Equip a ranged weapon and compatible ammunition or quiver. Maximum range starts at six tiles and increases by one tile for every ten Ranging levels. Perception improves damage and reduces distance loss.

You can keep shooting in melee, with reduced accuracy and damage. A distant hit can draw a creature towards you. Clicking the same target again stops shooting. The server resolves hit chance, damage, range and engagement.

entries.title: Armour and damage
entries.summary: Protection depends on the equipped piece and the attack
entries.body:
Equipment contributes the protection and modifiers shown in its item details and the Equipment window. Different attacks can deal physical or elemental damage; resistance and other effects can change the result.

Use the actual item details rather than judging protection by its appearance. Combat and damage are resolved by the server.

entries.title: How perks work
entries.summary: Pick points, tiers, exclusions and gear
entries.body:
A perk is bought with pick points, and most of them are bought more than once. There are 33 perks on the shelf and 33 of them come in tiers.

Pick points come from overall levels: two for each, spent on attributes, nexus or perks, and never spent twice. Every tier of a perk costs 3 pick points; most perks have three purchasable tiers, and Essence Keeper has five. Gold costs rise with each tier.

Some perks cannot be held together - Lucky Hitter and Lucky Dodger answer the same question from opposite sides, and so do Mirror and Life Stealing. The page for each perk says what it clashes with.

Worn gear can carry a perk. A cape does not simply grant one: it adds a tier up to the perk effect cap. Most perks need gear to reach tiers four and five. Essence Keeper can learn all five levels; its cape adds one level up to the 95% cap.

A removal stone takes back one tier and returns what that tier cost. At its highest tier a perk that says so can be switched off with the #perk command, which hands back the effect and not the pick points.

#list_perks names everything you hold, the tier you are at, and what that tier does.

categories.title: Harvesting
categories.summary: Resources, recommended levels, knowledge and tools
categories.intro: Browse resources for their recommended Harvesting level, knowledge and tool requirements. Levels affect gathering speed; they are not minimum unlock levels. Harvesting currently requires no research books.

entries.title: Harvesting
entries.summary: Nodes, levels, and why you stopped
entries.body:
The server controls which objects are resource nodes and what they yield. Resource requirements and your character determine whether gathering can proceed.

Click a node to start. The server reports when harvesting starts and stops. Moving, missing a tool, running out of space or another interruption can stop gathering. Search a resource name in the encyclopedia to find recipes that use it.
facts: clicking a node the server has described
moving, a full backpack, or the server

entries.title: Bags on the ground
entries.summary: What is dropped, and who may take it
entries.body:
Dropped goods appear in bags on the ground. Opening a bag requests its current contents from the server.

You must reach the bag tile to open it and pick up items. Other players can view the same bag. The server settles pickup requests and limits how much fits in your backpack and carrying capacity.

entries.title: Storage
entries.summary: What a storage keeper holds for you
entries.body:
Each character has storage held by the server. A storage keeper allows deposits and withdrawals. Use #storage view for a view-only preview from anywhere.

Withdrawals are checked against carrying capacity. The mixing window can draw materials from nearby storage; required tools must still be carried or equipped. Loot delivery and player payments can also involve storage, with the required approvals.

Enchanted equipment appears in a separate glowing stack. Open its item ledger to inspect the individual copies and effects. Enchanting, breaking down and recipes that consume equipment use exact backpack copies; withdraw the item and required materials first. See Equipment & Enchanting for the steps.

entries.title: Resource requirements
entries.summary: Levels, tools and yields
entries.body:
Browse the Harvesting topic for a page per resource with its recommended level, knowledge and tool requirements, and base experience. Use the Resources type filter to hide general guides, or sort by Level to plan what to gather.

The listed Harvesting level is a recommendation used for gathering speed, not a minimum level to start. Harvesting currently requires no research books. Any knowledge needed to make an item from a resource is shown on the recipe page instead. Required tools must be carried or equipped.

The live server controls resource nodes, gathering speed, rewards and interruptions. Each resource page links to recipes that use it. This client does not ship a complete per-resource location directory.

categories.title: Trade
categories.summary: Dealing with players and with the exchange
categories.intro: Two ways to move goods between people, both settled by the server.

entries.title: Trading and the exchange
entries.summary: Direct trades and the Nymara Exchange
entries.body:
A direct trade is between two players, and both must accept before anything moves. The server owns every step; the window shows what it has confirmed.

The Nymara Exchange takes listings and holds both goods and proceeds in escrow until they are collected.

entries.title: What a thing is worth
entries.summary: NPC prices, the exchange and player-set prices
entries.body:
NPC shop windows show their current buy and sell prices. Exchange listings and direct trades use their own offered prices. A recipe is a materials and requirements reference, rather than a market valuation.

Gauntlet loot can be assigned to individual players or split. The leader can set a price on eligible assigned items; payments use the storage approval flow before delivery. Personal rewards stay with their owner. Review quantities, prices and recipients before approving.

categories.title: Equipment & Enchanting
categories.summary: Individual copies, effect crafting, breakdown and essence refining
categories.intro: Craft an individual copy, enchant it with enriched essences, or break it down into materials for your next item. These guides describe the default rules; the live Review window checks your exact copy and current costs.

entries.title: Miniboss and final boss equipment
entries.summary: Blue and yellow equipment drops in gauntlets and the Serpent Deep raid

sections.title: A roll for each dropped copy
sections.text: Minibosses and final bosses in gauntlets and the Serpent Deep raid can drop equipment with saved effects. Each equipment copy rolls independently after the enemy's normal item drop roll. These chances do not guarantee that an enemy drops equipment. Blue copies start with one or two effects; yellow copies start with three or four.

sections.title: Inspect before sharing
sections.text:
Each enchanted copy has its own party-loot row, with a colored name, effect icons and effect descriptions. Click its item icon to inspect the saved effects and stats. The leader assigns each copy individually. Its identity and effects stay with it through storage delivery, party exchange sales and approved exchange withdrawals.

Ordinary enemies, chests, caches and completion-choice rewards keep their existing rules. Server settings can change the listed chances.

entries.body: Minibosses and final bosses in gauntlets and the Serpent Deep raid can drop equipment with saved effects. Each equipment copy rolls independently after the enemy's normal item drop roll. These chances do not guarantee that an enemy drops equipment. Blue copies start with one or two effects; yellow copies start with three or four.

entries.title: Equipment copies and effects
entries.summary: Instanced equipment, blue and yellow names, and choosing the right copy

sections.title: Your individual equipment
sections.text:
Every equippable item is an individual copy. Copies of the same item can have different effects, rolled values, quality, durability and creators. Plain copies may appear together in a stack; an enchanted copy keeps its own saved effects.

Blue names support up to two effects. Yellow names support up to four. Both stat bonuses and triggered effects count toward this limit. The windows show name color and effect slots rather than adding a rarity word to the item name.

sections.title: Find the exact copy
sections.text: The crafting windows list each backpack copy with its slot and effect count. Select a row to inspect its effects and condition. Enchanted items in storage have their own glowing stack; open the item ledger to inspect the individual copies. Withdraw a stored copy and unequip it before enchanting or breaking it down.

sections.title: Open the windows
sections.text: Use Inventory → ••• → Enchant equipment… or Break Down & Refine…, or the Enchant and Break Down actions on an equipment inspection card. Mixing offers Enchant equipment… in its ••• menu and a Refine button. The Break Down, Refine and Enchant tabs move between the windows. These entries appear when the connected server supports them.

sections.title: Review before spending
sections.text:
Select the copy and materials, then press the operation’s Review button. The server checks the exact copy, cost and room for the result before opening confirmation. Nothing is spent until you confirm. Changing a selection requires a new review.

The amounts and odds in these guides describe the current default rules. Use the live window’s review for your world’s current costs, chances and returns.

entries.body:

Blue names support up to two effects. Yellow names support up to four. Both stat bonuses and triggered effects count toward this limit. The windows show name color and effect slots rather than adding a rarity word to the item name.

entries.title: Crafting individual equipment
entries.summary: Rare crafting results, plain tutorial recipes and exact-copy ingredients

sections.title: Craft equipment in Mixing
sections.text:
Choose the item’s recipe in Mixing, gather its materials and meet the usual knowledge, skill and tool requirements. A successful eligible equipment recipe can create an enchanted copy with randomly chosen effects. Each result rolls its own effects.

These are the default chances for a successful eligible craft before Artificer and other rare-mix bonuses. The effect roll is separate from the chance that the recipe succeeds.

sections.title: Default equipment crafting results
rows: Blue name · one or two effects
Yellow name · three or four effects

sections.title: Tutorial crafting
sections.text: Tutorial crafting and recipes marked plain stay plain. Basic Quiver is also a plain result under the default rules. Complete the tutorial and use an eligible recipe or the Enchant window to obtain equipment with effects.

sections.title: Recipes that consume equipment
sections.text:
Withdraw the equipment and all recipe materials into your backpack first. Press Mix Now and select the exact equipment copies for one attempt. Check their slots, effects and condition before confirming. Automatic queues cannot choose equipment copies for you.

Success normally consumes the selected copies and other ingredients; ordinary failure keeps them. Critical failure can consume them. Recycler and loss-prevention perks follow the usual mixing rules. The exact copies selected are the ones at stake.

sections.title: Enchant an existing item
sections.text: To add effects to equipment you already own, open Enchant and choose that plain copy. This spends enriched essences on the selected item instead of creating a new item from a recipe.

entries.title: Enchanting plain equipment
entries.summary: Spend enriched essences to give a chosen plain copy one to four effects

sections.title: Choose a copy and an essence
sections.text:
Unequip the item and place it in your backpack. Open Enchant, select the plain copy, then choose an enriched essence theme and quantity. More options lets you combine essence themes. Spend one to five enriched essences in total.

The selected themes favor matching effects that are eligible for that item. The item keeps its identity, creator, quality and condition. Press Review enchantment, read the material cost and possible results, then confirm. The effects and their numbers are rolled after confirmation.

sections.title: Using more enriched essences
sections.text: Each enriched essence rolls the effect count once; the highest count wins. All selected essences are spent. More essences improve the chance of extra effects while keeping the same possible range for each effect’s numbers. The window updates the odds as you change the selection.

entries.title: Promoting, adding, removing and rerolling effects
entries.summary: Choose an operation for an already enchanted copy

sections.title: Work on the selected copy
sections.text: Open Enchant and select an unequipped backpack copy. The Operation selector offers the actions available for its current effects. Select an action, set its materials and any effect choices, then use Review to check the cost before confirming. These operations keep the copy’s quality, durability and creator.

sections.title: Promotion and additional effects
rows: A blue copy with exactly two effects costs 10 Enriched Magic Essence + 10 Enriched Life Essence. Both existing effects and their values stay, a third distinct effect is added, and the name becomes yellow.

A blue copy can fill its second slot for 1 Enriched Life Essence. On yellow copies, filling the second or third slot costs 1 each; filling the fourth costs 2. Existing rolls stay. Promote a full blue copy before adding more effects.

sections.title: Remove or reroll
rows: Spend 1 to remove a random effect, or 3 to remove the saved effect you choose. Other rolls stay. Removing the final effect makes the copy plain.
Spend 1–5 to keep the effect names and reroll their numbers. Each number keeps the best new roll from that many attempts. Existing values can decrease; name color and effect count stay.

Spend 1 to reroll all effects and numbers. Spend 3 to preserve up to one chosen effect, or 5 to preserve up to two. Preserved effects keep their numbers. Leave at least one effect unlocked. Name color and effect count stay.

sections.title: Optional effect themes
sections.text:
When promoting, adding effects or rerolling effect types, More options offers enriched Fire, Frost, Earth and Wind as optional themed catalysts. Spend up to five catalysts in total alongside the operation’s main cost. They favor eligible effects of their themes; the result is still random. Life additions and Magic effect rerolls also favor their own essence themes.

The default enchanting operations have no extra gold fee. The live review shows any fee configured for your world.

entries.body: Open Enchant and select an unequipped backpack copy. The Operation selector offers the actions available for its current effects. Select an action, set its materials and any effect choices, then use Review to check the cost before confirming. These operations keep the copy’s quality, durability and creator.

entries.title: Breaking down enchanted equipment
entries.summary: Salvage or disenchant one copy for universal Enchanting Shards and normal essences

sections.title: Choose the equipment to destroy
sections.text:
Unequip and withdraw the enchanted copy into your backpack. Open Break Down & Refine… and use the Break Down tab, or choose Break Down on its inspection card. Select the exact copy by backpack slot and inspect its current effects.

The window shows its exact returns and states that this individual copy will be destroyed. Press Review breakdown and confirm only when the selected copy and returns are the ones you want.

sections.title: Default returns per copy
rows: 2 Enchanting Shards + 5 normal essences in total
5 Enchanting Shards + 10 normal essences in total
10 Enchanting Shards + 20 normal essences in total
15 Enchanting Shards + 30 normal essences in total

sections.title: Which normal essences you receive
sections.text:
The normal-essence total is divided between the copy’s effects, and each effect supplies its assigned essence family. Shares assigned to the same family are combined. For example, a two-effect copy with Brutal and Flamebound returns 5 Earth Essence, 5 Fire Essence and 5 Enchanting Shards.

Returns use the number and families of the saved effects. The exact per-copy preview shows how whole essences are divided when the total does not divide evenly.

sections.title: Using the recovered materials
sections.text: Enchanting Shards are universal: they work with any supported normal essence in Refine. Build up shards and normal essences, then refine the family you want for enchanting. Plain equipment has no recoverable effects, and quest items cannot be broken down through this window. Make room to carry the returns before confirming.

The window shows its exact returns and states that this individual copy will be destroyed. Press Review breakdown and confirm only when the selected copy and returns are the ones you want.

entries.title: Creating normal and enriched essences
entries.summary: Alchemy and Potion recipes, rare enriched results and guaranteed refining

sections.title: Make normal essences
sections.text:
Find Life, Death, Water, Magic, Fire, Earth and Wind Essence recipes in Alchemy. Frost Essence recipes are in Potions and use the Potion skill. Search the essence name to see all its recipe alternatives.

The generated recipe page lists ingredients, tools, knowledge and the recommended skill level. Gather those materials and use the recipe in Mixing. Normal recipe success and failure rules apply. Breaking down enchanted equipment also returns normal essences. These normal essences are the matching-family material used by Refine.

sections.title: Two sources of enriched essences
sections.text:
Successful normal-essence mixes can produce an enriched essence as a rare result. The default base chance is 1 in 10,000 successful mixes before Artificer and other rare-mix bonuses. Tutorial mixes keep the normal result.

Refining is the guaranteed route: combine universal Enchanting Shards, normal essences of one family and a gold fee. Open Mixing → Refine or Inventory → ••• → Break Down & Refine… → Refine. Choose a recipe and quantity, check the Need and Owned columns, then press Refine to review and confirm.

sections.title: Default cost for one enriched essence
rows: 1 enriched essence of the same family
Guaranteed after confirmation; no manufacturing failure roll

sections.title: Refine more at once
sections.text: The default batch limit is 100. Every cost and the result scale with quantity: refining two costs 40 Enchanting Shards, 200 matching normal essences and 200 Gold Coins, and produces two enriched essences. Use materials from your backpack and leave room for the result. The live review shows your world’s configured costs, batch limit and gold fee.

entries.body:
Find Life, Death, Water, Magic, Fire, Earth and Wind Essence recipes in Alchemy. Frost Essence recipes are in Potions and use the Potion skill. Search the essence name to see all its recipe alternatives.

The generated recipe page lists ingredients, tools, knowledge and the recommended skill level. Gather those materials and use the recipe in Mixing. Normal recipe success and failure rules apply. Breaking down enchanted equipment also returns normal essences. These normal essences are the matching-family material used by Refine.

entries.title: Essence themes and recovered materials
entries.summary: What each enriched family favors and which normal essences effects return

sections.title: Choose a theme for enchanting
sections.text: Enriched essences favor effects that suit their family. An item can only receive effects eligible for its equipment type, and each new effect is distinct from effects already kept on that copy. Themes change the chances of eligible effects; they do not guarantee a named effect or increase its possible numeric range.

sections.title: Favored effects while enchanting
rows: Brutal, Sundering, Bodkin, Reinforced, Plated, Stoneward, Arrowguard
Balanced, Trueflight, Elusive, Lightweight, Second Wind

sections.title: Themes when breaking down
sections.text: Breaking down assigns each saved effect to one normal-essence family. This is a separate assignment from enchanting preferences: an effect can be favored by several enriched themes but return one normal family. For example, Siphoning returns Water Essence and Restorative returns Life Essence.

categories.title: Alchemy
categories.intro: Alchemy turns what is harvested into the essences and bars the other trades consume. For enriched essence creation, Enchanting Shards and refining, see Equipment & Enchanting → Creating normal and enriched essences.

categories.title: Manufacturing
categories.intro: Metal work. Armour is made in pieces - helm, torso, legs, boots and shield - and the same bars go into the weapons that beat them. Equipment results can carry individual effects; see Equipment & Enchanting → Crafting individual equipment for rare results and exact-copy ingredients.

categories.title: Crafting
categories.intro: Crafting wants a mould more often than it wants a fire. Equipment results can carry individual effects; see Equipment & Enchanting → Crafting individual equipment for rare results and exact-copy ingredients.

categories.title: Engineering
categories.intro: Things that are built rather than forged.

categories.title: Potions
categories.intro: A potion is mixed once and drunk once. What it does is the server's to apply.

categories.title: Tailoring
categories.intro: The longest recipe list in the client, and the one that most often wants a book first. Equipment results can carry individual effects; see Equipment & Enchanting → Crafting individual equipment for rare results and exact-copy ingredients.

categories.title: Summoning
categories.summary: Calling a creature to your side
categories.intro: A summoning is paid for in stones and flesh, and the creature that arrives is the server's, not yours.

categories.title: Magic
categories.summary: Sigils, spells and the effects they leave
categories.intro: Choose a spell family, targeting mode and Power 1–10. Higher power replaces separate greater spells.

entries.title: Casting and power
entries.summary: One effect, ten power levels
entries.body:
Learn the required spell-family tome, carry the reagents and choose a power your Magic level and Magic nexus support. Heal, Fire Bolt and Restore Ether need no tome. Higher power changes strength, duration or utility and can cost more ether and reagents.

The spell window can be searched and filtered by targeting mode. Generated spell pages list the unlock level, recommended level, base ether cost, nexus and Power 1 reagents. The live casting preview gives the exact cost at your chosen power.

entries.title: Self, Target, Allies and Burst
entries.summary: Choose who receives a spell
entries.body: A base name such as Heal affects you. Target selects one actor within 15 tiles; Bolt also means one target. Allies affects you and party or guild members within four tiles. Burst selects a location within 15 tiles and affects eligible actors within four tiles of it. Hostile spells respect party, guild and PK restrictions. Escape cancels target selection without spending resources.

entries.title: Damage, wards and Dispel
entries.summary: Match protection to the damage type
entries.body: Magic Bolt deals magic damage; Fire Bolt heat; Frost Bolt cold; Radiation Bolt radiation. Each has a Burst form and a matching ward. Elemental Ward combines heat, cold and radiation protection. Shield improves physical protection. Dispel removes poison, cripple, resistance reductions and drained stats. Magic Immunity temporarily blocks hostile spells.

entries.title: Transmute
entries.summary: Selected inventory items become gold
entries.body: Choose an inventory item and quantity. Review the required power and exact gold return before casting. Common items need Power 1, Uncommon 3, Rare 5, Epic 7 and Legendary 9. Their gold multipliers are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 times the item base transmutation value. Only the selected quantity is consumed. Gold Coins and quest items cannot be transmuted.

entries.title: Recall and portal destinations
entries.summary: Higher power opens destination selection
entries.body: Recall at Power 1–4 returns you to Four Gates. At Power 5–10 choose a map with a portal entrance and the entrance where you will arrive. Maps with several entrances list each location. Blink remains a short teleport to a walkable place within 15 tiles.

categories.title: Books
categories.summary: What must be read before it can be made
categories.intro: A book is read once. Until the server records that you have read it, the recipes it teaches are refused however high your level is.

categories.title: Maps
categories.intro: Each region is its own map on the server. Crossing between them is a change of map, not a walk across a seam.

entries.title: Finding chat commands
entries.summary: Use #help for the current command list
entries.body:
Type #help or #list for the commands available to you on the current server. The Help tab lists local controls and commands handled by this client. A command beginning with # that the client does not handle is sent to the server.

Useful reference commands include #storage view for a view-only storage preview, #research for current research progress, #list_quests for quest numbers and #list_knowledge for knowledge numbers. Reset commands require a repeated confirmation and can remove progress: read the server response before confirming.
